sections.html:
Warsaw is home to all three offices involved. Pick the right one from the table.

Benton County, MO property tax offices
OfficeWhat it handlesContact
AssessorValue of land, buildings and personal propertyP.O. Box 40, Warsaw; real estate 660-438-5323, personal property 660-438-5473
County ClerkHearing bookings, plus value and rate certificationP.O. Box 1238, Warsaw; 660-438-7326
CollectorBills, payments, duplicate paid receiptsP.O. Box 428, Warsaw; 660-438-7721

The Collector mails the bills and takes payment for the county as well as the cities of Warsaw, Lincoln, Cole Camp and Ionia. The Clerk passes certified values and rates to every taxing body.

Warsaw, the largest city and the seat, anchors Benton County in west central Missouri. Residents numbered 19,394 in 2020, and the 2025 estimate is 20,536. The median age is 53.8. Of the 13,551 housing units, 37.1% sat vacant in 2020, and 80.4% of occupied homes had their owners living in them.

Warsaw R-IX, Cole Camp R-I and Lincoln R-II serve the county, and your statement shows which one applies to you.

Value is pegged to January 1. The Benton County Assessor covers more than 32,000 parcels and over 12,000 personal property accounts. Houses and land get a full reassessment in odd years; in even years staff only hunt for new construction and buildings that were lost. That made 2026 a review year, with the next full reassessment in 2027.

Appraisers carry ID and drive marked county cars. They may view the outside of a property but can't go into a building, so the rest of the detail comes from questionnaires or an on-site chat with you.

Values must land within 10% of market under State Tax Commission rules, and an office that strays can lose state funding. The Assessor doesn't set the bill, since the taxing districts' levies do that.

If your notice looks high, take these steps.

  1. Ask for your Property Record Card and check the size, condition and description for mistakes.
  2. Point out any problem the office may not know about, such as damage or a poor layout.
  3. Offer an appraisal from a Missouri certified appraiser if you hold one.
  4. If the number holds, book a hearing with the County Clerk.
  5. Last, take the board's ruling to the Missouri State Tax Commission.

The Commission appeal comes from RSMo 138.430. Its deadline is September 30 of the assessment year, or thirty days after the board decides if that is later, and the decision letter goes with the filing. Entities such as an LLC, trust, association or estate must have an attorney file for them.

sections.h2: When Benton County bills are due
sections.html:
Look for your statement by Thanksgiving, and call the Collector if it hasn't come. You owe the amount when it arrives, but nothing turns delinquent until after December 31. A mailed check needs a postmark of December 31 or earlier, because a later one is sent back unless late fees are enclosed.

At the counter the office takes cash, a personal check or a credit card. The courthouse's north-side drop box stays open until midnight on December 31 with no penalty. One check can cover several statements, but wrong or partial amounts are refused.

Mailed payments are credited on the postmark date under RSMo 139.100. For 2026 bills, protect December 31, 2026.

Who owes the tax is decided on January 1. Even a seller who leaves the next day owes the year's bill, and state law has no proration rule.

So the contract has to divide the year between buyer and seller. Typically the title company deducts the seller's portion from the proceeds and pays the county or credits the buyer. Ring the Collector at 660-438-7721 before signing to learn the full balance, earlier years included.

A value error can't be fixed at the Collector's counter. Take it to the Assessor before you pay.

The same applies to a cash sale. With no lender escrow, the closing agent splits the year as the contract directs and pays the county from the proceeds. Ask the buyer early whether they want the bill paid at closing or left for them to pay by December 31.

Real estate with two years of unpaid tax goes to auction on the fourth Monday of August. Bidding happens outside the Warsaw courthouse, and the county's tax sale site lists the parcels.

Losing the auction doesn't end your claim right away. RSMo 140.405 obliges the winning bidder to send redemption notice by first class and certified mail no fewer than ninety days before a deed can be taken. Transferring or encumbering the land means redeeming it first.

To sell a delinquent parcel, get the full payoff to the Collector and the title company ahead of the auction. Once redeemed, it can close like any other house.

If you contest the bill, RSMo 139.031 allows full payment before the delinquency date together with a written statement of why and what value you claim. The Collector sends on the undisputed part and keeps the rest apart.

Sue the Collector in circuit court within ninety days of the protest, unless you already have a timely assessment appeal open with the State Tax Commission or a court. Tax paid by mistake can be refunded or credited if you ask within three years.

Personal property has its own date. Report what you owned on January 1 to the Assessor by March 1 to avoid penalties.

sections.h2: Before you list a Benton County home
sections.html:
A few phone calls up front keep a sale from stalling at the closing table.

  1. Call the Collector at 660-438-7721 and ask for the balance on the parcel, including any earlier year. A parcel with two years unpaid can head to the August auction.
  2. Call the Assessor at 660-438-5323 for real estate questions, or 660-438-5473 if a vehicle or other personal property account is involved. Ask whether the record card matches the house as it stands.
  3. If you plan to dispute the value, remember that the Clerk books Board of Equalization hearings at 660-438-7326.
  4. Tell the title company who gets the statement, since bills go to the owner on file. Mail sent to an old address still counts as your debt.

Keep your paid receipts. The Collector gives out duplicates if you lose one, which can save time when a buyer or lender asks for proof of payment on prior years. If the office is closed, you can still use the drop box on the north side of the courthouse for a December payment.

faqs.q: Where do I pay property tax in Benton County, Missouri?
faqs.a: Send it to the Collector at P.O. Box 428 in Warsaw, pay at the office, or use the courthouse's north-side drop box. For your parcel's current payoff, call 660-438-7721.

faqs.q: When do Benton County property taxes become delinquent?
faqs.a: Once December 31 ends. A check postmarked later comes back unless late fees are included, and the drop box takes payments until midnight that night.

faqs.q: Does Benton County reassess property every year?
faqs.a: No. Full reassessment happens in odd years, and even years only add new construction and remove lost improvements. The next full one is 2027.

faqs.q: When is the Benton County tax sale?
faqs.a: On the fourth Monday of August, at the courthouse in Warsaw, for real estate with two years of delinquent tax.

faqs.q: Is Benton County property tax prorated when I sell?
faqs.a: The law doesn't prorate it, and the January 1 owner stays liable for the year. Your sale contract sets the split, and the title company handles payment at closing.
